title: Cardinals overwhelm Dodgers 13-8 on September 2 with five-home-run offensive display
dek: St. Louis defeated Los Angeles 13-8 at Dodger Stadium with 13 hits and five home runs, scoring in six different innings. The Cardinals' offensive display came during the playoff-race stretch run.
author: The GoCheckMySports Desk
key_fact: Cardinals scored 13 runs on 13 hits, including five home runs, in a single game at Dodger Stadium on September 2.
bottom_line: The Cardinals enter the final weeks of the season on the strength of significant offensive depth. How that performance translates across the remaining regular-season games will determine whether the September 2 output signals a turning point in the pennant race or a single outlier.
body: The St. Louis Cardinals defeated the Los Angeles Dodgers 13-8 on September 2 at Dodger Stadium, delivering a record-breaking offensive performance that included 13 hits and five home runs, per MLB.com.

The Cardinals scored in six different innings, spreading their production across the game rather than relying on a single outburst. The offensive output reflects sustained pressure on Dodgers pitching throughout the night at Dodger Stadium during the final stretch of the regular season.

The 13 runs and 13 hits represent a historic offensive night for the Cardinals in a ballpark where scoring opportunities are typically limited. The five home runs underscored the Cardinals' ability to hit for power against Los Angeles pitching.
